title: Linux UDEV Rule Created
author: Raven Tait, Splunk
description: The following analytic detects the creation of files within udev rules directories, including /etc/udev/rules.d and /usr/lib/udev/rules.d. Adversaries abuse udev rules to achieve persistent code execution by embedding RUN+= directives that trigger arbitrary commands whenever a matching device event occurs, such as a USB device being connected or a network interface coming online. Because udev rules execute in the context of the udev daemon with elevated privileges, this technique can provide both persistence and privilege escalation. It is used by post-exploitation frameworks such as PANIX and is effective on headless servers where device events still fire despite no interactive user session.
